title: MedNeXt: Transformer-Driven Scaling of ConvNets for Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: ConvNeXt blocks throughout encoder and decoder with compound scaling, and UpKern: initialise a large-kernel network by upsampling the kernels of a trained 3x3 network.
adaptation: 2D MedNeXt-B/L k3 at 512 px, 1 channel, label-safe aug, then UpKern to k5. Large kernels give context for E1 (scuff v crack) without attention. 2D support in repo unverified; a 2D port of the block is small.
min_experiment: MedNeXt-B k3 and k5 (UpKern) 2D, 5 folds v nnU-Net arm A. Metric: CV crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill if no metric improves by >=0.01 (CV) or 0.03 (E1).
evidence: R (nnU-Net Revisited Table 1): MedNeXt L best on 5 of 6 3D sets (e.g. LiTS 82.34 v 80.09, ACDC 92.65 v 91.54) at 68-233 GPU-h; part of the gain attributed to target spacing.
prior_overlap: ConvNeXt-T encoder screen under PF (DINOv3 v ImageNet, 4k steps, F51) showed no sign of gain, but that compared pretraining, not a ConvNeXt U-Net with UpKern and long schedule. Open.
